newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two die, up to 20 hurt in Russian railway blast.
newsitem.headline: Two die, up to 20 hurt in Russian railway blast.

text.p: A powerful explosion tore through a railway station in the southern Russian town of Armavir on Wednesday, killing two people and wounding up to 20, local police said.
A police duty officer in the main regional city of Krasnodar said by telephone the blast had thrown parts of one of the bodies across the station in Armavir.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for the early evening blast, but Itar-Tass news agency said an explosive device may have gone off in a passenger's bag at the ticket office and identified one dead person as a man who may have been carrying it. A child was among the injured, it said.

Armavir is about 320 km (200 miles) from the separatist region of Chechnya, where some rebels have issued threats to stage attacks on Russian cities to commemorate the first anniversary of independence leader Dzhokhar Dudayev's death.

Separatist rebels staged two hostage-taking raids outside Chechnya during their almost 21-month conflict with Russia. A ceasefire was agreed last August but talks are bogged down over the region's demands for complete independence.
Tass said President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had been informed.
It quoted the regional security chief, Yevgeny Vorontsov, as saying a passenger train had been waiting just outside the station at the time of the blast.
